question.text: Under Section 115BBI read with Section 115BBC of the Income Tax Act, anonymous donations received by a charitable trust (other than a religious trust) in excess of the threshold are taxed at:

answer.text: 30% plus applicable surcharge and cess, on the amount exceeding the higher of INR 1 lakh or 5% of total donations
40% plus applicable surcharge and cess, on the full anonymous donation

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Section 115BBC levies tax @ 30% on anonymous donations exceeding the higher of (a) INR 1,00,000 or (b) 5% of total donations received in the year. Section 115BBI (inserted 2022) provides for tax @ 30% on various specified income of trusts including anonymous donations and non-application of 85%. **The Trap:** 10% and 20% are capital-gains or equity-dividend rates, not anonymous-donation. 40% overstates the rate and misrepresents the base (only excess over threshold is taxed, not the full donation). **Cross-Exam Context:** XXIV (AML) tests anonymous / suspicious transactions for reporting; XXIII tests the taxation consequence under 115BBC / 115BBI. The SIA must reconcile donor-register traceability to this threshold. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Flag in your SIA report: count of 'anonymous' receipts (no PAN, no address) and their aggregate. Compute the higher of INR 1 lakh or 5% of total donations — any excess triggers 30% tax and should be separately disclosed in the Notes to AIR for donor transparency.
